meta.title: The Record of Intent
meta.description: A curated register of statements bearing on intent: genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid, annexation, starvation and war crimes. Every entry is verbatim, attributed to a named speaker with role and date, and carries the source and a note on evidentiary significance. Statements by serving officials are admissions, not allegations.

primary_databases.name: Law for Palestine — Database of Israeli Incitement to Genocide
primary_databases.detail: 500+ instances catalogued from 7 October 2023, continuously updated; categorised by genocidal intent, forced displacement and collective punishment.

primary_databases.name: Al-Haq / Forensic Architecture Investigation Unit — A Registry of Israeli Genocidal Statements on Gaza
primary_databases.detail: 1,000+ instances of incitement and genocidal intent since 7 October 2023, thematically indexed.

primary_databases.name: Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor
primary_databases.detail: Independent verification and cataloguing of the most probative ministerial and military statements.

primary_databases.name: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT (A/HRC/60/CRP.3)
primary_databases.detail: 16 September 2025 — found Herzog, Netanyahu and Gallant incited genocide, and that genocidal intent was the only reasonable inference from the totality of the evidence.

categories.label: Genocidal intent
categories.blurb: Statements advanced as direct evidence of dolus specialis — the specific intent to destroy a protected group, in whole or in part, as such (Genocide Convention, Article II), or of direct and public incitement under Article III(c).

categories.label: Ethnic cleansing
categories.blurb: Statements of intent to remove the protected population from its territory — the war crime and crime against humanity of deportation or forcible transfer (Fourth Geneva Convention Article 49; Rome Statute Articles 7(1)(d) and 8(2)(b)(viii)).

categories.label: Dehumanisation
categories.blurb: The denial of the target population's humanity — treated in the Genocide Convention's travaux préparatoires and in ICTR jurisprudence as the paradigmatic precursor marker of genocidal intent.

categories.label: Targeting of children
categories.blurb: Statements endorsing the killing or removal of the group's children — among the gravest categories of genocidal intent, since destruction of a group's children destroys its capacity to reproduce itself.

categories.label: Siege and starvation
categories.blurb: Statements ordering or defending the deprivation of food, water, fuel and medicine — starvation of civilians as a method of warfare (Rome Statute Article 8(2)(b)(xxv)), the charge on which the ICC issued warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant in November 2024.

categories.label: Apartheid and discrimination
categories.blurb: Admissions of a two-tier legal and enforcement regime based on ethnicity — the actus reus of apartheid (Apartheid Convention 1973; Rome Statute Article 7(1)(j); CERD Article 3).

categories.label: Annexation and occupation
categories.blurb: Statements of intent to annex occupied territory or to entrench settlement — prohibited by the peremptory norm against acquisition of territory by force and by the ICJ Advisory Opinion of 19 July 2024.

categories.label: War crimes and collective punishment
categories.blurb: Statements ordering indiscriminate attack, disproportionate force or punishment of a population for acts it did not commit (Fourth Geneva Convention Article 33; Rome Statute Article 8).

categories.label: Extension beyond Gaza
categories.blurb: The explicit transposition of the Gaza template to Lebanon and the occupied West Bank — evidence both of intent toward a second population and, by admission, of the character of what was done in Gaza.

categories.label: Founding-era record
categories.blurb: Statements from the founding period of the movement and the state, establishing that transfer of the indigenous population was articulated as policy long before 1948.

categories.label: Societal incitement
categories.blurb: Population-scale evidence — polling and the Hebrew-language public record — that the intent documented at ministerial level is shared by a majority of the group from which the conscript army is drawn.

categories.label: Israeli and Jewish dissent
categories.blurb: Statements against interest: Israeli prime ministers, generals, attorneys general, historians and human rights organisations reaching the same legal characterisations. These foreclose the claim that only outside critics use these terms.

categories.label: Formal findings
categories.blurb: The determinations of courts, UN bodies and genocide-prevention institutions on the statements catalogued here.

categories.label: Jewish opposition to Zionism
categories.blurb: Religious, scholarly, organisational and public statements by Jewish individuals and bodies rejecting political Zionism or the conduct of the Israeli state. These bear on the conflation examined in Part XXI — whether opposition to Zionism is by its nature antisemitic — and on nothing else; no legal characterisation in the report depends on them. Part XXIII sets out the survey evidence on how small a minority these positions are among Jews today.

items.speaker: Ahad Ha'am (Asher Ginsberg)
items.quote: [Jewish settlers] treat the Arabs with hostility and cruelty, trespass unjustly upon their boundaries, beat them shamefully without reason, and even brag about it.
items.context: The essay “Truth from Eretz Yisrael”, written after a visit to Palestine six years before Herzl convened the First Zionist Congress.
items.source: Ahad Ha'am, “Truth from Eretz Yisrael”, 1891.
items.significance: A founding figure of the movement documenting the pattern before the movement had held its first congress. The ethical critique is internal to Zionism and predates it as an organised politics.

items.speaker: Theodor Herzl
items.quote: [A Jewish state in Palestine would form] a portion of a rampart of Europe against Asia, an outpost of civilization as opposed to barbarism.
items.context: Der Judenstaat, the founding pamphlet of political Zionism, published one year before the First Zionist Congress.
items.source: Theodor Herzl, Der Judenstaat, 1896.
items.significance: The explicit civilisational-colonial vocabulary common to European settlement projects of the period, in the movement's founding text.

items.speaker: Central Conference of American Rabbis
items.role: The rabbinic body of American Reform Judaism, then the largest Jewish denomination in the United States
items.quote: We totally disapprove of any attempt for the establishment of a Jewish state. Such attempts show a misunderstanding of Israel’s mission.
items.context: A unanimous declaration issued in response to the First Zionist Congress, convened by Theodor Herzl at Basel on 29–31 August 1897. The Union of American Hebrew Congregations resolved in parallel: “We are unalterably opposed to political Zionism. The Jews are not a nation, but a religious community… America is our Zion.” In Germany the rabbinic protest known as the Protestrabbiner was published in July 1897, urging Jews to abstain from the Congress.
items.source: Central Conference of American Rabbis, 1897; American Jewish Archives; Posen Library. Report §23.2.
items.significance: Institutional Jewish rejection of political Zionism at the moment of the movement’s founding, by the dominant American Jewish denomination of the day. It bears only on the claim that anti-Zionism and antisemitism are the same position.

items.speaker: Vladimir Jabotinsky
items.role: Founder of Revisionist Zionism; ideological forebear of Likud
items.quote: [Zionist settlement is] a colonising adventure [that will be resisted] as any indigenous people [would resist]… colonisation can have only one goal [and must proceed] regardless of the native population.
items.context: The essay “The Iron Wall (We and the Arabs)”, 1923.
items.source: Vladimir Jabotinsky, “The Iron Wall”, 1923; cited in Rashid Khalidi, The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020).
items.significance: The movement's own vocabulary for itself, from the founder of the tradition from which Likud descends. The colonial framing is not a later critical imposition; it is the self-description of the project by one of its architects.

items.speaker: David Ben-Gurion
items.role: Chairman of the Jewish Agency Executive; later first Prime Minister of Israel
items.quote: [Compulsory transfer is] an opportunity which we never dared to dream of in our wildest imaginings… national consolidation in a free homeland.
items.context: Diary entry on the compulsory transfer of Arabs proposed by the British Peel Commission. On 7 August 1937 he told the Zionist Assembly that in many parts of the country new settlement would not be possible without transferring the Arab fellahin. In a letter to his son the same year he wrote: “We must expel Arabs and take their place.”
items.source: Ben-Gurion diaries, 12 July 1937; 1937 Ben-Gurion letter; Benny Morris, The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem Revisited (2004).
items.significance: Establishes that transfer of the indigenous population was welcomed as policy by the movement's principal leader eleven years before 1948. Note the historiographical caution: a widely circulated variant (“The Arabs will have to go, but one needs an opportune moment…”) is contested as a paraphrase rendered as direct quotation. The diary and letter texts above are documented.

items.speaker: Arthur Ruppin
items.role: Head of the Zionist Organisation's Palestine Office; architect of Zionist land settlement
items.quote: I do not believe in the transfer of the individual, I believe in the transfer of entire [Palestinian] villages.
items.context: Statement to a Jewish Agency Executive meeting. On 29 October 1936, 21 members of the Jewish Agency Executive had endorsed a proposal to transfer displaced Arab farmers to Transjordan.
items.source: Jewish Agency Executive minutes, 1938; Institute for Palestine Studies.
items.significance: Transfer articulated by the movement's chief settlement planner as a collective, village-scale programme rather than individual relocation — the distinction that separates migration from ethnic cleansing.

items.speaker: American Council for Judaism
items.role: Founded by thirty-six Reform rabbis; Rabbi Louis Wolsey, chair; Rabbi Elmer Berger, executive director; Lessing Rosenwald, president
items.quote: [Judaism is] a religion of universal values, not a nationality; Palestine should become a democratic state in which all citizens hold equal political rights irrespective of religion.
items.context: Constituted after a meeting at Atlantic City on 1 June 1942 opposing the CCAR resolution of February 1942 supporting a Jewish army in Palestine, which the dissenting rabbis regarded as a breach of the movement’s stated neutrality of 1935. The organisation was named at a meeting in New York on 7 December 1942. The position lost: the Reform movement had already reversed itself in the Columbus Platform of 1937, and the Council was marginalised after 1948.
items.source: Thomas A. Kolsky, Jews Against Zionism: The American Council for Judaism, 1942–1948 (Temple University Press, 1990); Jewish Virtual Library. Report §23.2.
items.significance: The programme is summarised rather than quoted verbatim from a single document. Recorded as the last organised institutional expression of classical Reform anti-Zionism before the establishment of the state.

items.speaker: Yitzhak Yezernitzky (Yitzhak Shamir)
items.role: Lehi operations commander; later Prime Minister of Israel (1983-1984, 1986-1992)
items.quote: Neither Jewish ethics nor Jewish tradition can disqualify terrorism as a means of combat. We are very far from having any moral qualms as far as our national war goes.
items.context: From an article titled “Terror” published in the Lehi underground journal HeHazit (The Front) in the summer of 1943, republished in translation by MERIP as a documentary source in May 1988, which attributes it to Yezernitzky. Translations of the passage vary in wording, and some sources attribute the article to the journal without naming an author. Lehi was designated and suppressed as a terrorist organisation by the British Mandatory authorities.
items.source: MERIP, “Document: Shamir on Terrorism (1943)”, May 1988
items.significance: The founding organisations' own description of their method. It is the first limb of the argument at Part XXIV: the characterisation is not applied retrospectively by critics but adopted contemporaneously by the organisation whose commander later led the state.

items.speaker: Albert Einstein, Hannah Arendt, Sidney Hook and others
items.quote: [Herut is] a political party closely akin in its organization, methods, political philosophy and social appeal to the Nazi and Fascist parties.
items.context: Open letter to the New York Times on Menachem Begin's US tour, eight months after Deir Yassin and two months after Herut was founded as the Irgun's political successor. Herut's successor organisation, via Gahal, is Likud.
items.source: The New York Times, 4 December 1948.
items.significance: Not a retrospective comparison but a contemporaneous assessment, published three years after the liberation of the Nazi camps, by Zionism's most eminent physicist and one of the century's most serious political philosophers — both Jewish — about the direct political ancestor of the governing party.

items.speaker: Moshe Dayan
items.quote: Jewish villages were built in the place of Arab villages. You do not even know the names of these Arab villages, and I do not blame you because geography books no longer exist. Not only do the books not exist, the Arab villages are not there either… There is not a single place built in this country that did not have a former Arab population.
items.context: Address to students at the Technion, Haifa, 19 March 1969; transcript published in Haaretz on 4 April 1969 and later quoted in Edward Said, The Question of Palestine (1980).
items.source: Haaretz, 4 April 1969; Edward Said, The Question of Palestine (1980).
items.significance: The Haaretz citation is undisputed across both critical and defensive sources. The context is contested: CAMERA renders a fuller passage in which Dayan also refers to land purchased from Arabs, and argues the remarks concerned Jezreel Valley settlements founded 1921–27 rather than villages depopulated in 1948. The quotation is included here with that dispute stated, consistent with this record's practice of flagging contested provenance rather than omitting or overstating.

items.speaker: Golda Meir
items.quote: There was no such thing as Palestinians. When was there an independent Palestinian people with a Palestinian state? … It was not as though there was a Palestinian people in Palestine considering itself as a Palestinian people and we came and threw them out and took their country from them.
items.context: Interview with Frank Giles, deputy editor of The Sunday Times, published 15 June 1969 under the headline “Who can blame Israel”, marking the second anniversary of the 1967 war. Later in the same interview she said: “I don't say there are no Palestinians. But I say there is no such thing as a distinct Palestinian people.”
items.source: The Sunday Times, 15 June 1969; cited in Rashid Khalidi, The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020) and Edward Said, The Question of Palestine (1980).
items.significance: The canonical statement of national-identity denial by a serving Israeli prime minister. Dov Waxman treats it as the most famous Israeli expression of the denial of a distinct Palestinian identity; Khalidi argues it takes the negation characteristic of a settler-colonial project to its highest possible level. Denial of the group's existence is a recognised precursor marker in genocide scholarship, and the same move recurs in Smotrich (2017) and Wasserlauf (2025).

items.speaker: Yitzhak Rabin
items.quote: [Israel risks becoming an apartheid state if it annexes and absorbs the West Bank's Arab population.]
items.context: Warning issued during his first premiership.
items.source: Contemporaneous Israeli press, 1976; collated in Israeli apartheid scholarship.
items.significance: The earliest of the prime-ministerial apartheid warnings. Note the tense: Israeli leaders have consistently reserved the label for an unspecified future, never the present — but the criterion they name (a single political entity in which the Palestinian population cannot vote) has been satisfied for decades.

items.speaker: Lt. Gen. Rafael Eitan
items.role: Chief of the General Staff of the IDF (1978–1983)
items.quote: When we have settled the land, all the Arabs will be able to do about it will be to scurry around like drugged cockroaches in a bottle.
items.context: Reported by Gad Becker in Yediot Ahronot, 13 April 1983, and carried by The New York Times on 14 April 1983, at the end of Eitan's tenure as Chief of the General Staff.
items.source: Yediot Ahronot, 13 April 1983 (Gad Becker); The New York Times, 14 April 1983.
items.significance: Insect metaphor from the serving head of the armed forces, tying dehumanisation directly to settlement as the mechanism of subjugation. The same vermin register recurs forty years later in the ministerial record of 2023–2026 (“human animals”, “subhumans”, “not even people”). Of the three most-circulated historical dehumanisation quotations, this is the one with a traceable contemporaneous press source; the Begin “two-legged beasts” and Shamir “grasshoppers” attributions are disputed as to wording and referent and are therefore not relied on here.

items.speaker: Yitzhak Rabin
items.quote: [Ordering soldiers to] break their bones.
items.context: Instruction to Israeli forces confronting stone-throwing during the First Intifada. Over 1,000 Palestinians, including 237 children, were killed by Israeli forces in the period 1987–1993.
items.source: Contemporaneous Israeli and international press, January 1988; B'Tselem.
items.significance: An explicit ministerial order to inflict permanent injury on children as a policy of deterrence. Rabin received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994. The order is the direct doctrinal ancestor of the “limping monuments” policy Maj. Gen. Bluth described in 2026.

items.speaker: Ilan Pappé
items.role: Israeli historian, University of Exeter; formerly University of Haifa
items.quote: [The 1948 expulsion of the Palestinians was] an ethnic cleansing operation [planned in advance and executed systematically.]
items.context: The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine (Oneworld, 2006), drawing on Israeli state and military archives, including Plan Dalet (March 1948).
items.source: Ilan Pappé, The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine (2006).
items.significance: Most historians in Israel and abroad no longer dispute that Israeli forces expelled large numbers of Palestinians in 1948 and barred their return; the continuing debate is over whether it was centrally preconceived. Benny Morris — who rejects Pappé's framing — nonetheless documents the expulsions in detail in The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem Revisited (2004).

items.speaker: Ehud Olmert
items.quote: [If the two-state solution collapses, Israel will] face a South African-style struggle for equal voting rights, and as soon as that happens, the state of Israel is finished.
items.context: Remarks to Israeli media immediately after the failure of the Annapolis conference.
items.source: Haaretz; The Guardian, November 2007.
items.significance: A serving prime minister naming the South African comparison as the consequence of the status quo he was administering.

items.speaker: Maj. Gen. Gadi Eisenkot
items.role: IDF Northern Command (later Chief of the General Staff)
items.quote: What happened in the Dahiya quarter of Beirut in 2006 will happen in every village from which Israel is fired on. […] We will apply disproportionate force on it… From our standpoint, these are not civilian villages, they are military bases.
items.context: Interview with Yedioth Ahronoth setting out what became known as the Dahiya Doctrine.
items.source: Yedioth Ahronoth, October 2008; cited in the UN Goldstone Report (A/HRC/12/48, 2009).
items.significance: A doctrine of deliberate disproportionality against civilian infrastructure, stated openly by a serving general and reclassifying civilian villages as military objectives. The Goldstone Report treated it as evidence that disproportionate destruction was policy rather than error — the doctrinal ancestor of the conduct documented in Gaza after 2023.

items.speaker: Avi Shlaim
items.role: Emeritus Professor of International Relations, University of Oxford; Fellow of the British Academy; served in the Israeli army in the mid-1960s
items.quote: My definition of ‘terror’ is the use of violence against civilians for political purposes.
items.context: Interviewed on Democracy Now! during Israel's Gaza offensive. Asked to define terror, Shlaim gave the definition above and then applied it in both directions in the same answer: by that definition Hamas is a terrorist organisation, and Israel “is practicing state terror”. He added that he holds no brief for Hamas, which is “not a paragon of virtue”, and that killing civilians is wrong whoever does it.
items.source: Democracy Now!, 14 January 2009
items.significance: The methodological point at §24.1 and §24.4, made by an Israeli historian: a single definition is stated before the actors are named and then applied to whoever meets it. An actor-based definition that exempts states decides the question before the evidence is heard.

items.speaker: Ehud Barak
items.role: Prime Minister of Israel (1999); Defence Minister (2010)
items.quote: As long as in this territory west of the Jordan River there is only one political entity called Israel it is going to be either non-Jewish, or non-democratic. If this bloc of millions of Palestinians cannot vote, that will be an apartheid state.
items.context: Herzliya security conference, as serving Defence Minister. He had made the same argument as Prime Minister in 1999.
items.source: Haaretz, 2 February 2010.
items.significance: The criterion is stated by a former prime minister and serving defence minister: one political entity, millions who cannot vote. Both conditions were already satisfied when he said it, and remain so.

items.speaker: Avraham Shalom
items.quote: We have become cruel, to ourselves as well, but mainly to the occupied population, using the excuse of the war on terror.
items.context: Speaking in Dror Moreh's documentary The Gatekeepers (2012), in which six former directors of the Shin Bet - Shalom, Ami Ayalon, Yaakov Peri, Carmi Gillon, Avi Dichter and Yuval Diskin - spoke collectively on the record for the first time. Shalom also compared the force he had served in to an occupying army of the Second World War. Carmi Gillon, another of the six, said: “We are making the lives of millions unbearable, into prolonged human suffering.”
items.source: The Gatekeepers (dir. Dror Moreh, 2012)
items.significance: Testimony from the head of the agency that ran the policy, describing its effect on the occupied population and the function of the counter-terrorism justification. A statement against the speaker's own institution and career.

items.speaker: Michael Ben-Yair
items.quote: [Israel has imposed] an apartheid regime [on the West Bank.]
items.context: Public call urging the European Union to endorse a Palestinian state. Ben-Yair had earlier written that the occupation created “an apartheid regime in the occupied territories”.
items.source: Israeli and European press, November 2014.
items.significance: The state's own former chief legal officer applying the term in the present tense, not the conditional future used by the prime ministers.

items.speaker: Meir Dagan
items.quote: [Continuing Netanyahu's policies will result in an Israel that is] either a binational state or an apartheid state.
items.context: Public intervention ahead of the 2015 Israeli election.
items.source: Israeli press, 2015.
items.significance: The head of Israel's foreign intelligence service for nine years reaching the same binary as Barak and Rabin.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: [The Palestinian people are] an invention of less than a hundred years.
items.context: Statement made before entering government; repeated in substance since.
items.source: Israeli media, 2017; cited by genocide scholars as precursor speech.
items.significance: Denial of the existence of the national group is listed by genocide scholars among the standard precursor markers: a group that does not exist cannot be destroyed, and cannot claim the protection of the Convention.

items.speaker: Avigdor Lieberman
items.quote: There are no innocent people in the Gaza Strip.
items.context: Said on Israeli public radio after ten days of the Great March of Return, in which Israeli snipers had killed about thirty demonstrators at the perimeter fence. Lieberman added that everyone in Gaza is connected to Hamas and receives a salary from Hamas, and that those approaching the fence were operatives of its military wing.
items.source: AFP and The Jerusalem Post, 16 April 2018, reporting remarks made the previous day.
items.significance: The collective-guilt formula that became routine after October 2023 was ministerial language five years earlier, and was applied then to unarmed demonstrators. It is recorded here with its correct date because it circulated widely in late 2023 as though it had been said during the current war: the statement is real, the 30 November 2023 date attached to it in viral posts is not.

items.speaker: Lod District Court (Israel)
items.role: Israeli district court, sentencing in the Duma arson case
items.quote: Extreme and racist ideology.
items.context: The court's characterisation of the motive of Amiram Ben-Uliel, convicted of three counts of murder, two of attempted murder and conspiracy for the firebombing of the Dawabsheh family home in Duma on 31 July 2015, which killed 18-month-old Ali Dawabsheh outright and both his parents of their burns. The offences were classified as a terrorist act; he received three life sentences and twenty further years. He was acquitted of membership of a terrorist organisation. The Supreme Court dismissed his appeal in 2022, finding “no doubt” that he had committed the “shocking and deeply disturbing” attack. A crowdfunding campaign for his release later raised more than NIS 1.2 million, and a petition to improve his prison conditions was signed by fourteen coalition lawmakers.
items.source: Lod District Court and Supreme Court of Israel; The Times of Israel
items.significance: “Jewish terrorism” is an Israeli judicial and institutional category, not an external characterisation. The state's judicial organ names the conduct terrorism; parts of the state's political organ campaign for the man convicted of it. That division is the sponsorship element of the fourth limb at §24.2, documented internally.

items.speaker: B'Tselem
items.role: Israeli Information Center for Human Rights in the Occupied Territories
items.quote: This is not democracy plus occupation. This is apartheid between the river and the sea.
items.context: Position paper “This is Apartheid: A Regime of Jewish Supremacy from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea”. The quotation is from then-director Hagai El-Ad. The paper identifies one organising principle behind Israeli policy: advancing and perpetuating the supremacy of one group — Jews — over another — Palestinians — across all territory Israel controls.
items.source: B'Tselem, 12 January 2021.
items.significance: The leading Israeli human rights organisation applying the apartheid finding to the whole territory, including within the Green Line, and grounding it in Basic Law: Israel — the Nation State of the Jewish People. B'Tselem reached the genocide determination in July 2025 in “Our Genocide”.

items.speaker: Human Rights Watch
items.quote: [Israeli authorities are committing] the crimes against humanity of apartheid and persecution.
items.context: Report “A Threshold Crossed: Israeli Authorities and the Crimes of Apartheid and Persecution”, the first of the three major apartheid findings by internationally mandated organisations (with B'Tselem, January 2021, and Amnesty International, February 2022).
items.source: Human Rights Watch, “A Threshold Crossed”, 27 April 2021.
items.significance: Establishes the two-element test applied since: an intent to maintain domination by one racial group over another, plus systematic oppression and inhumane acts. HRW reached the genocide determination in December 2024 and called the ICJ's July 2024 findings on apartheid “a wake-up call”.

items.speaker: Amnesty International
items.quote: [Israel maintains] a system of oppression and domination [over Palestinians, meeting the international legal definition of apartheid.]
items.context: 278-page report compiled over four years, following Human Rights Watch's “A Threshold Crossed” (April 2021) and B'Tselem's January 2021 paper.
items.source: Amnesty International, “Israel's Apartheid Against Palestinians”, 1 February 2022.
items.significance: B'Tselem said the report “marks a new consensus, recognizing the fact that Israel employs a regime of Jewish supremacy between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.” Amnesty reached the genocide determination in December 2024.

items.speaker: 104 human rights organisations
items.role: Open letter to the UN Secretary-General and the High Representative for the UN Alliance of Civilizations
items.quote: [The IHRA definition] has often been used to wrongly label criticism of Israel as antisemitic, and thus chill and sometimes suppress, non-violent protest, activism and speech critical of Israel and/or Zionism.
items.context: Letter to António Guterres and Miguel Ángel Moratinos urging the United Nations not to endorse or adopt the IHRA working definition in its action plan on monitoring antisemitism. Sixty organisations signed on 3 April 2023; the list had grown to 104 by 20 April. The letter opens from the premise that antisemitism “poses real harm to Jewish communities around the world and requires meaningful action to combat it”, and objects to the instrument rather than the aim: UN action must not “inadvertently embolden or endorse policies and laws that undermine fundamental human rights”. It names the Jerusalem Declaration on Antisemitism and the Nexus Document as alternatives. Signatories include Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, the ACLU, Al-Haq, the Cairo Institute for Human Rights Studies and FIDH, together with the Israeli organisations B'Tselem and Breaking the Silence and the American Jewish organisation Americans for Peace Now.
items.source: Human Rights Watch, 4 and 20 April 2023; Amnesty International, April 2023.
items.significance: The objection to the definition is not advanced only from outside the community the definition exists to protect. The counter-record is stated alongside it at §21.9: a letter of 17 May 2023 signed by more than 160 Jewish communal and civil society organisations calls the definition “an indispensable tool to understand and fight antisemitism”, “one that can be used entirely consistently with fundamental human rights standards”.

items.speaker: Tally Gotliv
items.quote: Bring down buildings! Bomb without distinction!! Stop with this impotence. You have ability. There is worldwide legitimacy! Flatten Gaza. Without mercy! This time, there is no room for mercy.
items.context: Posted on the day of the attack.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor.
items.significance: “Bomb without distinction” is an express call to abandon the principle of distinction — the foundational rule of international humanitarian law and the definition of an indiscriminate attack under Article 8 of the Rome Statute.

items.speaker: Ariel Kallner
items.quote: Nakba to the enemy now! This day is our Pearl Harbor. We will still learn the lessons. Right now, one goal: Nakba! A Nakba that will overshadow the Nakba of 48. A Nakba in Gaza and a Nakba for anyone who dares to join.
items.context: Posted the day after 7 October.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: The explicit naming of the 1948 expulsion as the declared goal, with the stated ambition of exceeding it. The 1948 Nakba expelled some 750,000 Palestinians; “overshadowing” it in a territory of 2.3 million describes a scale of removal that can only be achieved by destruction.

items.speaker: Nissim Vaturi
items.quote: Erase Gaza. Nothing else will satisfy us. It is not acceptable that we maintain a terrorist authority next to Israel. Don't leave a child there — expel everyone.
items.context: Subsequently: referred to Gazans as “subhumans” (February 2025); called to “burn Gaza” and “kill all adult men” (March 2025); posted an image of bombed Gaza captioned “no Arabs no terror problems” (September 2025); and on Channel 14 (c. June 2026), of the West Bank: “Jewish Israelis will not be able to live here in peace until we expel all the Arabs from this area. There should not be any Arabs there at all.”
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Israeli media, 2023–2026.
items.significance: The Knesset Ethics Committee ruled in February 2025 that calling Palestinians “subhumans” and calling to “kill all adult men” did not violate Knesset ethical standards — a formal institutional finding that genocidal incitement is within the bounds of acceptable legislative speech.

items.speaker: Yoav Gallant
items.quote: I have ordered a complete siege on the Gaza Strip. There will be no electricity, no food, no fuel, everything is closed. We are fighting human animals, and we are acting accordingly.
items.context: Announcement of the total siege, two days after 7 October.
items.source: Israeli Ministry of Defence statement, 9 October 2023; cited in South Africa v. Israel, ICJ.
items.significance: The single most cited statement in the case. It couples an order to deprive a civilian population of the means of life with the explicit denial of that population's humanity — the actus reus of Article II(c) of the Genocide Convention (deliberate infliction of conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction) stated together with its mens rea. The ICC issued an arrest warrant against Gallant for starvation as a method of warfare on 21 November 2024.

items.speaker: Yoav Kisch
items.quote: Those are animals, they have no right to exist. I am not debating the way it will happen, but they need to be exterminated… until we see hundreds of thousands fleeing Gaza, we, the IDF has not achieved its mission.
items.context: Public remarks, 9 October 2023.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: Three of the five principal markers of genocidal intent identified in ICJ and ICTR jurisprudence in a single statement: dehumanisation, an express call for extermination, and forced mass displacement stated as a defined mission objective. The speaker is the minister responsible for the formation of Israeli children.

items.speaker: Maj. Gen. Ghassan Alian
items.role: Head of COGAT (Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories)
items.quote: Human animals must be treated as such. There will be no electricity and no water, there will only be destruction. You wanted hell, you will get hell.
items.context: Video statement in Arabic, addressed directly to the population of Gaza.
items.source: COGAT official channels, 10 October 2023.
items.significance: The officer in command of the body that administers the movement of goods and people into Gaza, stating that deprivation of water and electricity is the policy and that the population is not human. The statement is directly probative both of the actus reus of Article II(c) and of the mens rea.

items.speaker: Rear Admiral Daniel Hagari
items.role: Chief Spokesperson of the Israel Defense Forces
items.quote: The emphasis is on damage and not on accuracy.
items.context: A briefing to Israeli military correspondents on the third day of the air campaign, reported the same morning by Haaretz's live blog. In the same briefing Hagari said thousands of munitions had been dropped in twenty-four hours, at five times the rate of the 2006 Lebanon war.
items.source: Haaretz live blog, 10 October 2023, reported in English by Middle East Eye and Common Dreams the same day.
items.significance: An operational statement rather than a political one: the declared criterion of target selection is the scale of destruction rather than the discrimination between military objectives and civilians, which is the distinction Article 48 of Additional Protocol I requires. The dispute over it is recorded with it — the briefing was in Hebrew, the English renderings are translations, and HonestReporting argues the sentence is a paraphrase of Hagari's words rather than a verbatim quotation. No Israeli correction of the Haaretz report was issued.

items.speaker: Yoav Gallant
items.quote: Gaza won't return to what it was before. We will eliminate everything.
items.context: Address to Israeli forces on the Gaza perimeter.
items.source: Israeli media, 10 October 2023; cited by the UN Commission of Inquiry, September 2025.
items.significance: “Everything” is not a military objective. The statement describes an outcome — the elimination of a place and the conditions of its collective life — rather than the defeat of an armed force.

items.speaker: Ezra Yachin
items.role: Reservist mobilised by the IDF to address troops; veteran of the Lehi militia and of the Deir Yassin massacre of April 1948
items.quote: Be triumphant and finish them off, and don't leave anyone behind. Erase the memory of them.
items.context: Yachin, then 95, was called up five days after 7 October and driven in an army vehicle, in uniform, to address units before the ground invasion. He had lectured to the army for fifty years; the IDF's chief rabbi promoted him to First Sergeant in 2018.
items.source: Read to the International Court of Justice by advocate Tembeka Ngcukaitobi for South Africa, 11 January 2024; reported by Middle East Eye and the World Socialist Web Site.
items.significance: South Africa advanced it not as the view of one old man but as evidence of what the army chose to transmit to soldiers on the eve of the ground operation: the state selected the speaker, supplied the transport and the platform, and the address was made to units about to enter Gaza.

items.speaker: Israel Katz
items.role: Economy Minister (later Foreign Minister, then Defence Minister)
items.quote: Humanitarian aid to Gaza? No electrical switch will be turned on, no water hydrant will be opened, and no fuel truck will enter Gaza until the Israeli abductees are returned. No one will preach morals to us.
items.context: Statement on the total blockade.
items.source: Israeli media, 12 October 2023; Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor.
items.significance: Deprivation of electricity, water and fuel expressly tied to a political demand is collective punishment under Article 33 of the Fourth Geneva Convention. The statement anticipates by thirteen months the ICC's charge of starvation as a method of warfare against Netanyahu and Gallant.

items.speaker: Isaac Herzog
items.quote: It is an entire nation out there that is responsible. It is not true this rhetoric about civilians not aware, not involved. It's absolutely not true. They could've risen up, they could have fought against that evil regime.
items.context: Press conference, Tel Aviv.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; multiple Israeli outlets, 13 October 2023.
items.significance: The head of state extending criminal responsibility to an entire civilian population, and expressly rejecting the category of the uninvolved civilian, is the collapse of the distinction on which the whole of international humanitarian law rests. Central to the UN Commission of Inquiry's finding that Herzog engaged in direct and public incitement to genocide.

items.speaker: May Golan
items.role: Minister for the Advancement of the Status of Women
items.quote: I don't care about Gaza. I literally don't care at all. They can go out and swim in the sea. I want to see dead bodies of terrorists around Gaza. […] I am personally proud of the ruins of Gaza.
items.context: Public remarks and subsequent statement.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Israeli media, October 2023.
items.significance: Explicit indifference to the destruction of a civilian population, including its women and children, from the minister with statutory responsibility for protecting women from violence — and stated pride in the physical ruin of the territory.

items.speaker: Galit Distel-Atbaryan
items.quote: Erase all of Gaza from the face of the earth.
items.context: Public statement, October 2023.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: Erasure of a place, not defeat of a force. Cited among the ministerial statements catalogued in South Africa's ICJ application.

items.speaker: Meirav Ben-Ari
items.role: Member of Knesset (Yesh Atid, the main opposition party)
items.quote: The children of Gaza have brought this upon themselves.
items.context: Said in the Knesset chamber during a debate in which the Palestinian member Aida Touma-Sliman noted that more than nine hundred children had been killed by Israeli bombing in nine days. Ben-Ari first heckled that there is no symmetry, then took the floor to repeat it.
items.source: Knesset session video of 16 October 2023, timestamped and translated by Jonathan Ofir for Mondoweiss; republished by Truthout. The National rendered the line as “The children of Gaza brought it upon themselves.”
items.significance: The speaker sits for the liberal opposition rather than the governing right, which is why the statement is included: the attribution of responsibility to the victim group's children was not confined to the coalition. The two English renderings are independent translations of the same Hebrew sentence.

items.speaker: Almog Cohen
items.quote: Destroy a neighborhood in Gaza everyday the abductees are in their hands. If we blink, we run out of global credit. Every day that the abductees are with them, a neighborhood must be destroyed on its inhabitants.
items.context: Public statement.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor.
items.significance: An explicit call for the destruction of civilian neighbourhoods on a rolling schedule, tied to a political demand, “on its inhabitants” — collective punishment expressly prohibited by Article 33 of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

items.speaker: Tally Gotliv
items.quote: Without hunger and thirst among the Gazan population, we will not succeed in recruiting collaborators, we will not succeed in recruiting intelligence, or in bribing people with food, drink, medicine, in order to obtain intelligence.
items.context: Public statement. Gotliv separately said: “Without a Hiroshima-style attack, the war's objective will not be achieved.”
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor; Israeli press, October 2023.
items.significance: The explicit statement that mass civilian hunger and thirst are instruments of intelligence collection — combined with the total blockade imposed from 2 March 2025 — is directly probative of starvation as a deliberate method of warfare.

items.speaker: Ohad Tal
items.quote: We cannot go back to the same conception… we need to exact a territorial price from them, including returning Jewish settlements at least to the north of Gaza Strip.
items.context: Public statement, three weeks into the campaign.
items.source: Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor.
items.significance: Resettlement of Gaza stated as an objective while the population was still being displaced. Transfer of the occupying power's civilian population into occupied territory is a war crime under Article 49(6) of the Fourth Geneva Convention and Article 8(2)(b)(viii) of the Rome Statute.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: You must remember what Amalek did to you, says our Holy Bible. And we do remember.
items.context: National broadcast on the launch of the ground invasion of Gaza. The reference is to 1 Samuel 15:3: “Now go, attack the Amalekites and totally destroy all that belongs to them. Do not spare them; put to death men and women, children and infants, cattle and sheep, camels and donkeys.”
items.source: National broadcast, 28 October 2023; cited in South Africa's ICJ application, the UN Commission of Inquiry and the IAGS resolution.
items.significance: The invocation of a scriptural injunction to total annihilation, including infants, by a serving head of government at the moment of invasion. Cited as direct incitement to genocide by the UN Commission of Inquiry, the International Association of Genocide Scholars and South Africa's ICJ submission.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: We will encourage voluntary transfer of all Gazan citizens. We will offer them the opportunity to move to other countries because that land belongs to us.
items.context: Public remarks. Ben-Gvir also distributed weapons to settler militias; he was sanctioned in June 2025 by the UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Norway.
items.source: Israeli media, 2023; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: The territorial claim (“that land belongs to us”) supplies the purpose that removes the voluntariness from “voluntary transfer”. Population removal to secure title to territory is the definition of ethnic cleansing.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: There are no uninvolved civilians in Gaza.
items.context: Repeated publicly through the campaign. Smotrich was sanctioned in June 2025 by the UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Norway.
items.source: Israeli media, 2023; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: The denial of civilian status to an entire population of 2.3 million, of whom roughly half are children, is the precondition for treating the whole of it as a lawful target.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: This is the war between the sons of light and the sons of darkness. We will not let up on our mission until the light overcomes the darkness.
items.context: A letter to Israeli soldiers and officers, published on the Prime Minister's own account, which opened by repeating the Amalek verse — “Remember what Amalek did to you” — that he had used in his televised address of 28 October.
items.source: Letter of 3 November 2023, reported by The Jerusalem Post; translated in Al-Haq's compilation “Statements by Israeli Officials, Soldiers and Civil Society on Genocide”, January 2024.
items.significance: The phrase is from the Qumran War Scroll and describes a war of annihilation between two peoples rather than a campaign against an armed group. Its significance here is the audience and the pairing: it was addressed to the troops carrying out the operation, in the same document as the Amalek reference that South Africa placed before the International Court of Justice.

items.speaker: Amichai Eliyahu
items.quote: [Asked whether Israel should drop a nuclear bomb on Gaza:] That's one way.
items.context: Radio Kol Barama interview. Eliyahu was suspended from cabinet meetings but not dismissed.
items.source: Israeli radio, 5 November 2023; international wire coverage.
items.significance: A serving minister treating the nuclear annihilation of 2.3 million people as an available policy option. The absence of dismissal is itself evidence: the state declined to treat the statement as disqualifying.

items.speaker: Yitzhak Kroizer
items.quote: The Gaza Strip should be flattened, and there should be one sentence for everyone there — death. […] We have to wipe the Gaza Strip off the map. […] There are no innocents there.
items.context: Said in an interview on Galey Israel radio a month into the campaign, by a member of the governing coalition.
items.source: Galey Israel, 5 November 2023; official translation in Al-Haq's compilation “Statements by Israeli Officials, Soldiers and Civil Society on Genocide”, January 2024.
items.significance: A call for the death of the entire population of a territory, made by a serving legislator of a coalition party. Direct and public incitement to commit genocide is a separate offence under Article III(c) of the Genocide Convention, complete whether or not genocide follows. Kroizer was appointed chair of a Knesset committee in August 2025.

items.speaker: Avi Dichter
items.role: Agriculture Minister; former Director of the Shin Bet
items.quote: [This is] Gaza Nakba 2023.
items.context: Interview on Israeli television describing the operation.
items.source: Israeli television, November 2023; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: A serving minister and former head of the internal security service naming the operation after the 1948 expulsion of 750,000 Palestinians. The comparison is not made by critics; it is made by the government.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: [Letter to Israeli soldiers invoking the biblical war of total annihilation.]
items.context: A letter written to Israeli soldiers in November 2023 comparing the Gaza operation to what the UN Commission of Inquiry describes as a “holy war of total annihilation” in the Hebrew Bible.
items.source: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT, A/HRC/60/CRP.3, 16 September 2025.
items.significance: Cited by the Commission of Inquiry as part of the evidentiary basis for its finding that Netanyahu personally engaged in direct and public incitement to commit genocide.

items.speaker: Maj. Gen. (res.) Giora Eiland
items.role: Former head of Israel's National Security Council; adviser to the Defence Minister during the campaign
items.quote: Severe epidemics in the south of the Gaza Strip will bring victory closer.
items.context: From an article headed “Let us not be intimidated by the world”, published in the Hebrew edition of Yedioth Ahronoth while the international agencies were warning that the collapse of water and sanitation would produce exactly such epidemics. Eiland had earlier argued that the population of northern Gaza should be given the choice of leaving or starving.
items.source: Yedioth Ahronoth, November 2023; translated and reported by The New Arab and others.
items.significance: Disease is treated as an instrument of the campaign rather than a consequence to be mitigated. Article II(c) of the Genocide Convention covers deliberately inflicting on a group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction, and the author is a former national security adviser writing in the country's largest-circulation paper, not an anonymous account.

items.speaker: Masha Gessen
items.role: Staff writer, The New Yorker; descendant of Holocaust survivors
items.quote: For the last seventeen years, Gaza has been a hyperdensely populated, impoverished, walled-in compound where only a small fraction of the population had the right to leave for even a short amount of time — in other words, a ghetto.
items.context: From the essay “In the Shadow of the Holocaust”. The Heinrich Böll Foundation, in agreement with the Bremen Senate, withdrew from awarding Gessen the Hannah Arendt Prize for Political Thought on the basis of the essay; the prize was conferred in a reduced ceremony on 15 December 2023.
items.source: The New Yorker, 9 December 2023; Jewish Telegraphic Agency; Democracy Now!, 15 December 2023. Report §23.3.
items.significance: An instance of the pattern recorded in Part XXI: a comparison drawn by a Jewish writer descended from Holocaust survivors, treated as disqualifying by an institution charged with honouring Hannah Arendt.

items.speaker: Law for Palestine
items.quote: 500+ instances of Israeli incitement to genocide.
items.context: Database compiled from 7 October 2023, drawn from social media posts, television interviews and official statements by Israeli politicians, army personnel, journalists and other influential figures. Categorised by genocidal intent, forced displacement and collective punishment.
items.source: Law for Palestine, 4 January 2024; ReliefWeb; TRT World.
items.significance: The organisation notes that much of the evidence originates from the upper echelons of the Israeli government — the President, the Prime Minister, members of the Knesset, military personnel and law enforcement. It leaves the legal determination to the courts.

items.speaker: International Court of Justice
items.role: Principal judicial organ of the United Nations
items.quote: [Israel must] take all measures within its power to prevent and punish the direct and public incitement to commit genocide in relation to members of the Palestinian group in the Gaza Strip.
items.context: Provisional measures order in South Africa v. Israel, finding it plausible that the acts complained of fall within the Genocide Convention. Measures were strengthened on 28 March and 24 May 2024.
items.source: ICJ, Order of 26 January 2024, South Africa v. Israel.
items.significance: The Court ordered Israel to punish incitement — an order that presupposes incitement was occurring. Under Bosnia v. Serbia (2007) the duty to prevent genocide binds every state party from the moment it learns of a serious risk; this order is that trigger date. The UN Commission of Inquiry found in September 2025 that Israeli authorities had failed to take action against Herzog, Netanyahu and Gallant — that is, that the order was not complied with.

items.speaker: Jonathan Glazer
items.role: Director, The Zone of Interest; accepting the Academy Award for Best International Feature
items.quote: Right now we stand here as men who refute their Jewishness and the Holocaust being hijacked by an occupation, which has led to conflict for so many innocent people — whether the victims of October the 7th in Israel or the ongoing attack on Gaza.
items.context: More than a thousand Jewish figures in the film industry signed an open letter denouncing the speech; more than 150 others, among them Joaquin Phoenix, Joel Coen, Nan Goldin, Tom Stoppard and Elliott Gould, signed a letter in support. Both letters are recorded, because the division rather than either letter is the documented fact.
items.source: The Hollywood Reporter; Variety; Times of Israel, March–April 2024. Report §23.4.
items.significance: Contested within the community it came from. It is recorded for the narrow proposition that the objection to the invocation of the Holocaust in defence of the conduct is itself made by Jews.

items.speaker: Francesca Albanese
items.role: UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967
items.quote: [There are reasonable grounds to believe that the threshold indicating Israel's commission of genocide has been met.]
items.context: Report to the Human Rights Council, “Anatomy of a Genocide” (A/HRC/55/73). Albanese was subsequently sanctioned by the United States.
items.source: UN Special Rapporteur, “Anatomy of a Genocide”, A/HRC/55/73, March 2024.
items.significance: The first UN mandate-holder report to reach the genocide threshold, eighteen months before the Commission of Inquiry. Special Rapporteur on the right to food Michael Fakhri reached the same conclusion on starvation grounds in February 2025.

items.speaker: Naomi Klein
items.role: Writer; Professor of Climate Justice, University of British Columbia
items.quote: Too many of our people are worshipping a false idol once again… That false idol is called Zionism. [It] has taken the idea of the promised land and turned it into a deed of sale for a militaristic ethnostate… [it] has betrayed every Jewish value, including the value we place on questioning.
items.context: Delivered at the “Seder in the Streets to Stop Arming Israel” at Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, organised by Jewish Voice for Peace on the second night of Passover. Published by The Guardian on 24 April 2024 as “We need an exodus from Zionism”.
items.source: The Guardian, 24 April 2024. Report §23.4.
items.significance: A theological rather than political rejection, framed from inside the Passover liturgy — the argument that Zionism betrays Judaism rather than expressing it.

items.speaker: Al-Haq Forensic Architecture Investigation Unit
items.quote: A Registry of Israeli Genocidal Statements on Gaza — over 1,000 instances of incitement and genocidal intent documented since 7 October 2023.
items.context: Thematically indexed by incitement and intent, forced displacement, and collective punishment.
items.source: Al-Haq FAI Unit, alhaq.org/FAI-Unit/26257.html.
items.significance: The largest structured public register of the statement record; twice the size of the Law for Palestine database and independently compiled.

items.speaker: Gabor Maté
items.role: Physician and author; infant survivor of the Budapest ghetto
items.quote: What Israel is doing in Gaza is energetically almost identical to what the Nazis did.
items.context: Given in an interview with the journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin. The comparison rests on this interview; it is recorded as his testimony, not as a finding of the report, and no legal characterisation in Part VI depends on it. Maté has repeated the substance in interviews with The Real News Network and Al Jazeera (Centre Stage, 26 June 2025).
items.source: Interview with Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, 2024; The Real News Network; Al Jazeera, 26 June 2025. Report §23.3.
items.significance: Single-sourced to one interview and flagged as such. Its weight is that of a survivor’s testimony about what the comparison is for, not of a legal or historical finding.

items.speaker: International Court of Justice
items.role: Principal judicial organ of the United Nations
items.quote: [Israel's legislation and measures] impose and serve to maintain a near-complete separation in the West Bank and East Jerusalem between the settler and Palestinian communities [and] constitute a breach of Article 3 of CERD.
items.context: Advisory Opinion on the Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, paragraph 229. Article 3 of CERD addresses “two particularly severe forms of racial discrimination: racial segregation and apartheid” (para. 225). The Court found the occupation unlawful and ordered it ended as rapidly as possible, all settlements dismantled, full reparations paid and displaced Palestinians allowed to return.
items.source: ICJ Advisory Opinion, 19 July 2024, paras. 224–229; separate opinions of Judges Nolte, Iwasawa and Tladi.
items.significance: The Court found the breach without expressly qualifying it as apartheid rather than segregation, leaving both open. Most judges agreed the actus reus of apartheid was made out; they divided on the mens rea. Judge Tladi found it difficult to see how the systemic character of the acts could fail to reveal a purpose of domination. Human Rights Watch called the findings on apartheid and reparations a wake-up call.

items.speaker: Hanoch Milwidsky
items.quote: Yes! If he is a Nukhba, everything is legitimate to do! Everything!
items.context: Shouted in the Knesset after military police detained nine soldiers on suspicion of raping a Palestinian detainee at Sde Teiman, an assault that left the detainee with a ruptured bowel, broken ribs and lung damage. Milwidsky had walked out of a Finance Committee vote in protest at the arrests, depriving the committee of its quorum, and was asked by Hadash-Ta’al MK Ahmad Tibi whether it was legitimate to insert an object into a detainee’s rectum. The Jerusalem Post renders the reply more briefly as “If he is a Nukhba, everything is legitimate.”
items.source: CBS News, 30 July 2024; Jerusalem Post, 29–30 July 2024; Al Jazeera, 9 August 2024.
items.significance: A public defence of the rape of a detainee, conditioned only on the detainee’s asserted designation. The prohibition of torture is absolute and non-derogable: Article 2(2) of the Convention against Torture admits “no exceptional circumstances whatsoever”, and rape of a person in custody is a war crime under Article 8(2)(b)(xxii) of the Rome Statute and a crime against humanity under Article 7(1)(g) when committed as part of a widespread or systematic attack. Recorded at §15.13A alongside §10.3.

items.speaker: Anonymous IDF officer
items.role: Serving Israeli officer, quoted in a Haaretz investigation
items.quote: In Gaza, human shields are used by Israeli soldiers at least six times a day… almost every platoon [keeps a Palestinian detainee for this purpose].
items.context: Haaretz investigation documenting the systematic use of Gazans to clear tunnels and houses, and reporting that IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi was aware of the practice.
items.source: Haaretz, 13 August 2024.
items.significance: The use of protected persons to shield military operations is a war crime under Article 8(2)(b)(xxiii) of the Rome Statute. The testimony comes from within the force, and establishes command awareness.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: [Calling for the] total annihilation [of Gaza, invoking the biblical injunction against Amalek.]
items.context: Public remarks, August 2024.
items.source: Israeli media; Al Jazeera, August 2024.
items.significance: A serving finance minister naming comprehensive physical destruction of the territory as the intended outcome, and grounding it in the same Amalek injunction invoked by the prime minister.

items.speaker: International Criminal Court, Pre-Trial Chamber I
items.quote: [There are reasonable grounds to believe that Netanyahu and Gallant bear criminal responsibility for] the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare [and crimes against humanity of murder, persecution and other inhumane acts.]
items.context: Arrest warrants issued against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, and against Hamas commander Mohammed Deif.
items.source: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I, 21 November 2024.
items.significance: The first ICC arrest warrants against the sitting leadership of a state closely allied to the Western powers. The starvation charge maps directly onto the siege orders of 9 and 12 October 2023 catalogued in this register.

items.speaker: Yesh Din
items.role: Israeli human rights organisation — Volunteers for Human Rights
items.quote: [Over 93 per cent of investigations into settler violence against Palestinians are closed without indictment.]
items.context: Yesh Din's continuous monitoring of Israeli police files on ideologically motivated offences by Israeli civilians against Palestinians in the West Bank, maintained since 2005.
items.source: Yesh Din, law enforcement data sheets, 2005–2026.
items.significance: Non-enforcement measured over two decades by an Israeli organisation using Israeli police data. Systematic impunity for violence by one group against another, administered by the same state, is the enforcement limb of the apartheid finding and corroborates Maj. Gen. Bluth's May 2026 admission that the open-fire policy “involves discrimination”.

items.speaker: Moshe Ya'alon
items.role: Former IDF Chief of Staff; Minister of Defence, 2013-2016
items.quote: The road we are being led down is conquest, annexation and ethnic cleansing.
items.context: Interview with Democrat TV, followed by remarks to Kan and Reshet Bet. Asked what he meant, Ya'alon pointed to northern Gaza: “There is no Beit Lahia, there is no Beit Hanoun. They are operating in Jabalia and are essentially clearing the area of Arabs.” He refused to retract under pressure, said he based the claim on information from commanders in the field, added that “at the end of the day, war crimes are being committed”, rejected the claim that the IDF is the most moral army in the world, and said the ICC warrants were justified and that he would have issued them long ago against Smotrich and Ben-Gvir. He attributed the policy to the political leadership rather than to the military. The IDF Spokesman denied the accusations; Likud called them “slanderous lies”.
items.source: Democrat TV and Kan, reported 1-2 December 2024
items.significance: A former Chief of Staff and Defence Minister applying the terms ethnic cleansing and war crimes to operations he is in a position to characterise, and naming serving ministers as the proper subjects of ICC warrants.

items.speaker: Donald J. Trump
items.quote: The US will take over the Gaza Strip, and we will do a job with it too… We'll own it… Level the site, and get rid of the destroyed buildings, level it out, create an economic development…
items.context: White House press conference alongside Prime Minister Netanyahu, during the ceasefire, proposing to redevelop Gaza as “the Riviera of the Middle East” and to relocate its population. He hinted US forces could be deployed “if necessary”, and on 11 February said the US would simply “have” and “keep” Gaza.
items.source: Al Jazeera; CNN; NPR; Fortune, 5 February 2025.
items.significance: UN officials said the plan would amount to ethnic cleansing. Defence Minister Israel Katz welcomed it and ordered the army to prepare for the “voluntary departure” of Gazans — the same euphemism Communications Minister Karhi has admitted means coerced departure. The plan supplies the external political cover on which Katz's September 2026 statement (“Trump has not canceled it; he has frozen it”) expressly relies.

items.speaker: Geocartography Knowledge Group / Penn State University
items.role: Survey of 1,005 Jewish Israeli respondents, March 2025
items.quote: 82 per cent support the forced expulsion of the entire Palestinian population of Gaza; 47 per cent answered yes when asked whether the Israeli army should act as the biblical Israelites did under Joshua at Jericho — that is, kill all the inhabitants of a conquered city.
items.context: Also: 56 per cent support the expulsion of Arab citizens of Israel (up from 45 per cent in 2003); among Jewish Israelis under 40, 66 per cent support expelling Palestinian citizens and 58 per cent support repeating the Jericho conquest; only 2 per cent believe too much firepower has been used on Gaza.
items.source: Published in Haaretz; Geopolitical Economy Report, 30 May 2025; Middle East Eye; Genocide Watch; TRT World.
items.significance: Population-level evidence of specific intent, cross-tabulated by age, gender and political affiliation, collected during the events it measures. The generational figures indicate the consensus is strengthening, not decaying.

items.speaker: Hana Bendcowsky
items.role: Director, Jerusalem Center for Jewish-Christian Relations, Rossing Center
items.quote: Being the majority and having our own state comes with responsibilities.
items.context: On the release of the 2024 annual report, which documented 111 incidents. Bendcowsky added that the incidents the Center is able to track “barely scratch the surface of what happens”, and that “the phenomenon has increased in numbers, and the seriousness of the incidents has increased”. An accompanying survey found 36 per cent of Christians in Israel considering emigration, rising to 48 per cent among those under 30.
items.source: The Times of Israel, 27 March 2025
items.significance: States the standard the Israeli monitoring organisation applies to its own society, and the qualification it records on improved reporting. See section 3.5A.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: Read my lips: not a single grain of wheat will enter Gaza.
items.context: Responding to a Yedioth Ahronoth report that the Israeli army was preparing to resume aid entry without a prisoner-exchange agreement. He added: “It's astonishing that the IDF communicates with us through the media.” Israel had closed all crossings on 2 March 2025.
items.source: Israel National News; Ynetnews; NPR; Press TV, April 2025.
items.significance: The finance minister publicly asserting a veto over the entry of food into a besieged territory, at a moment when the IPC assessed nearly half a million people facing starvation. In August 2026 Smotrich approved the transfer of $50 million to an American aid fund while stating, of Gaza's population, “I don't care about the Gazans… What matters to me is the complete victory and destruction of Hamas.”

items.speaker: Breaking the Silence
items.role: Israeli veterans' organisation — testimony of an IDF Captain, Armored Corps, southern Gaza
items.quote: We decided on a line which is the borderline, past which everyone is a suspect, but it's not clear to me how familiar Palestinians are with this line.
items.context: From “The Perimeter: Soldiers' testimonies from the Gaza Buffer Zone 2023–2024”, based on interviews with dozens of soldiers. The report documents the razing of roughly 16% of the Gaza Strip to create a buffer zone at least a kilometre deep: “The mission given to soldiers in the field… was to create an empty, completely flat expanse about a kilometer wide along the Gaza side of the border fence.”
items.source: Breaking the Silence, “The Perimeter”, April 2025.
items.significance: A kill zone whose boundary the population it kills has no way of knowing. The soldiers' own account establishes that the destruction was systematic and ordered, not incidental to fighting. Later testimony collected by the organisation describes “retrospective incrimination” — seeking evidence connecting the dead to Hamas after a strike, in order to justify it.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: Gaza will be entirely destroyed [and Palestinians will] leave in great numbers to third countries.
items.context: Public remarks setting out the objective of the renewed offensive.
items.source: Al Jazeera, 6 May 2025.
items.significance: Destruction and depopulation stated together as a single intended outcome — the clearest ministerial articulation of the causal chain the ICJ was asked to consider.

items.speaker: Michal Waldiger
items.quote: There are no uninvolved in Gaza. […] [Of the children:] Yes, they will also have to kill them, because there is no choice. […] It is a shame that what's been done in Gaza didn't get worse.
items.context: Knesset plenum, in a heated exchange responding to Hadash-Ta'al MK Ahmad Tibi's condemnation of the killing of children in Gaza.
items.source: Middle East Eye, 13 May 2025; Israeli and international media.
items.significance: A serving member of a governing-coalition party, on the floor of the national legislature, endorsing the killing of the protected group's children as unavoidable. A widely circulated paraphrase — “No one is innocent in Gaza. Yes, children should be killed too. There is no other way.” — condenses these sourced remarks; translations vary, the substance does not.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: We are destroying more and more houses [so that Palestinians] have nowhere to return… the only obvious result will be Gazans choosing to emigrate outside of the Strip… but our main problem is finding countries to take them in.
items.context: Closed-door testimony to Knesset members, subsequently reported.
items.source: Times of Israel liveblog, May 2025; International Commission of Jurists analysis.
items.significance: The International Commission of Jurists characterised the statements as support for forced displacement. Former UK Supreme Court justice Lord Sumption said they would be likely to substantiate a case of genocidal intent. The admission is that destruction of housing is not incidental to combat but instrumental to depopulation.

items.speaker: Moshe Feiglin
items.role: Leader of the Zehut party; former Deputy Speaker of the Knesset
items.quote: The enemy is not Hamas… Every child, every baby in Gaza is an enemy. […] [Gaza must be] occupied as well as settled [and] not a single child should remain. […] Every child of this kind to whom you're giving milk now — in 15 years will rape your daughters and slaughter your sons.
items.context: Interview on Israel's Channel 14.
items.source: Middle East Eye; TRT World; Antiwar.com; Maariv, May 2025.
items.significance: Characterising every Gazan child and infant as an enemy, and demanding that “not a single child should remain”, is an open articulation of intent to destroy the group through its children. Action on Armed Violence cited the remarks in calling for Feiglin to be sanctioned by the United Kingdom.

items.speaker: Shlomo Karhi
items.quote: 'Voluntary' is at times a state you impose [on someone] until they give their consent.
items.context: Defending the policy of “voluntary migration” of Palestinians from Gaza.
items.source: Israeli media, 2025.
items.significance: The single most damaging admission in the forcible-transfer record: a serving minister conceding that the word doing all the legal work in the government's position means coercion. It removes the principal fig-leaf relied on to distinguish “encouraged emigration” from deportation under Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

items.speaker: Avi Shlaim
items.role: Emeritus Professor of International Relations, University of Oxford; Israeli historian and former Israeli soldier; Fellow of the British Academy
items.quote: Israel refuses to allow humanitarian aid to civilians and uses starvation as a weapon of war. If that’s not genocide, I don’t know what is.
items.context: Shlaim served in the Israeli army in the mid-1960s and describes his position as having changed through archival research. He has also said: “I now think there is no longer a meaningful distinction between Israel proper and Israel in the West Bank. It’s apartheid and Jewish supremacy.” His collection Genocide in Gaza: Israel’s Long War on Palestine was published by Irish Pages Press in 2024.
items.source: Jacobin, July 2025; Journal of Holy Land and Palestine Studies, 2025–2026; Avi Shlaim, Genocide in Gaza (Irish Pages Press, 2024). Report §23.3.
items.significance: An Israeli historian of the New Historians school, decorated by the British Academy, applying both the apartheid and the genocide characterisations on the basis of the archival and documentary record.

items.speaker: Israeli public opinion
items.role: Survey cited by the Times of Israel
items.quote: 65 per cent of Jewish Israelis believe the IDF is held back from achieving its military objectives by adherence to the principle of minimising unnecessary killing and harm to civilians.
items.context: Cited alongside the finding that IDF soldiers are “rarely punished for posting content online” regardless of what the content documents.
items.source: Times of Israel, 2025.
items.significance: A majority regarding the law of armed conflict itself as the obstacle. This is the societal counterpart to the ministerial statements: the constraint, not the killing, is what is resented.

items.speaker: Israel Katz
items.quote: [The military is to prepare a] humanitarian city [on the ruins of Rafah; an initial 600,000 displaced Palestinians from al-Mawasi would enter within 60 days of a ceasefire, and eventually the whole population of Gaza. Those admitted] would not be allowed to leave.
items.context: A briefing to Israeli reporters on 7 July 2025. Entry was to be conditional on individual security screening, the perimeter sealed by the military, and departure permitted only by emigration from Gaza, which Katz said in the same briefing he intended to advance. Rafah was demolished in preparation: satellite imagery analysed by Al Jazeera showed destroyed buildings rising from about 15,800 on 4 April 2025 to about 28,600 on 4 July 2025.
items.source: Briefing to Israeli reporters, 7 July 2025; The Guardian; The Times of Israel; Al Jazeera satellite analysis, 13 July 2025. Report §6.3A.
items.significance: A ministerial plan to concentrate a protected population in a closed zone from which departure is barred save by leaving the territory engages Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention and Articles 7(1)(d) and 7(1)(e) of the Rome Statute. It was stopped from inside: the military's own lawyers advised it would be unlawful, sixteen Israeli law academics called any order to advance it manifestly illegal, and the Chief of the General Staff declined to adopt it.

items.speaker: Ehud Olmert
items.quote: It is a concentration camp. I am sorry. … If they will be deported into the new 'humanitarian city', then you can say that this is part of an ethnic cleansing.
items.context: Interview with The Guardian, published 13 July 2025, on Israel Katz's plan for a sealed zone at Rafah. Olmert was precise about the limits of his own claim: he did not regard the campaign as then conducted as ethnic cleansing, because temporary evacuation away from hostilities is lawful and people had returned to areas where operations had ended. It was the sealed city that would mark the escalation, and the stated humanitarian purpose that he called “not credible”. The Prime Minister's Office replied by calling him “a convicted felon disgracing Israel on CNN”.
items.source: The Guardian, 13 July 2025; CNN, 14 July 2025; The Times of Israel. Report §6.3A, §21.8.
items.significance: A former Israeli prime minister applying the term whose use of Israel is treated, under the IHRA definition's illustration on Nazi comparisons, as the paradigm case of antisemitism. A description does not change its character according to who utters it.

items.speaker: Yair Lapid
items.role: Leader of the Opposition; Prime Minister of Israel, 2022
items.quote: I don't prefer to describe a humanitarian city as a concentration camp, but if exiting it is prohibited, then it is a concentration camp.
items.context: Israeli Army Radio, the same day as Olmert's interview, on the same plan.
items.source: Israeli Army Radio, 13 July 2025; The Times of Israel. Report §6.3A, §21.8.
items.significance: The conditional form is the point: the sitting leader of the Israeli opposition accepted the characterisation on the plan's own stated terms, the bar on leaving being the plan's defining feature.

items.speaker: Physicians for Human Rights Israel
items.quote: [Israel's systematic destruction of Gaza's health system constitutes an act of genocide.]
items.context: Report published in the same month as B'Tselem's “Our Genocide” — the first time two Israeli human rights organisations reached the genocide determination simultaneously.
items.source: Physicians for Human Rights Israel, July 2025; B'Tselem, “Our Genocide”, July 2025.
items.significance: The genocide finding reached from inside Israeli civil society by the profession best placed to assess the destruction of a health system. Weighted heavily in this record because it cannot be attributed to hostility to Israel's existence.

items.speaker: Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir
items.role: Chief of the General Staff, Israel Defense Forces
items.quote: [The army] does not impose forced population expulsions inside or outside the Gaza Strip.
items.context: A statement by the Chief of the General Staff's office to Israel's High Court of Justice, after Zamir declined to adopt the Rafah plan on the ground that it formed no part of the military's operational plan. The Wall Street Journal reported that military lawyers had advised him the plan would be unlawful if civilians were coerced into the zone and prevented from leaving.
items.source: Israel's High Court of Justice, July 2025; The Wall Street Journal; The Times of Israel. Report §6.3A.
items.significance: A statement against the plan by the officer who would have had to execute it, and the operative reason it was shelved.
