It also fixes the legal standard the Israeli military applied to itself in court, against which the conduct documented elsewhere in this record is to be measured.

items.speaker: Yuli Novak
items.quote: Nothing prepares you for the realization that you are part of a society committing genocide.
items.context: On the publication of B'Tselem's report “Our Genocide”, issued the same day as a separate report by Physicians for Human Rights-Israel - the first time two leading Israeli human rights organisations concluded that Israel is committing genocide. The report's central finding is that Israel's policy in Gaza, its outcomes and the statements of senior Israeli politicians and military commanders “lead us to the unequivocal conclusion that Israel is taking coordinated action to intentionally destroy Palestinian society in the Gaza Strip”, and that this has enjoyed “support, legitimization, and normalization from the majority of Jewish-Israelis, as well as from the Israeli legal system”. Outreach director Sarit Michaeli called it “the textbook definition of genocide”.
items.source: B'Tselem, “Our Genocide”, 28 July 2025
items.significance: A finding made by an Israeli organisation about Israeli society, including its own legal system. B'Tselem had made the equivalent move on the previous term in January 2021, four months before Human Rights Watch adopted the apartheid finding.

items.speaker: aChord Center, Hebrew University of Jerusalem
items.quote: 76 per cent of Jewish Israelis agree or partially agree that there are no innocents in Gaza.
items.context: Among coalition voters the figure was 87 per cent; among centrist voters 67 per cent; among left-wing voters 30 per cent. 92 per cent of Arab citizens of Israel rejected the claim.
items.source: aChord Center, Hebrew University; Haaretz; Middle East Eye, August 2025.
items.significance: The belief that a population of 2.3 million, roughly half of them children, contains no innocents is the definitional precondition for genocide. When three-quarters of the national group from which a conscript army is drawn holds that belief, the specific intent is not confined to political leadership.

items.speaker: Maj. Gen. Aharon Haliva
items.role: Director of the IDF Military Intelligence Directorate, 2021–2024
items.quote: For everything that happened on October 7, for every one person on October 7, 50 Palestinians must die. […] The fact that there are already 50,000 dead in Gaza is necessary and required for future generations. […] There is no choice — every now and then, they need a Nakba in order to feel the price.
items.context: Leaked recording of a closed briefing to colleagues, published by Channel 12 in August 2025. Haliva resigned in April 2024, the first senior IDF officer to resign over responsibility for the 7 October failures.
items.source: Channel 12, August 2025; UN Commission of Inquiry; Law for Palestine database.
items.significance: Three findings follow. First, an explicitly adopted 50:1 killing ratio is directly probative of specific intent. Second, describing 50,000 deaths as “necessary and required” forecloses any claim that the scale results from military necessity rather than policy. Third, invoking the Nakba as a template for periodic repetition is direct evidence of the intent element. Made in a closed briefing, not for public consumption.

items.speaker: International Association of Genocide Scholars
items.role: The principal professional body of genocide scholarship
items.quote: [Israel's actions in Gaza meet the legal definition of genocide under the 1948 Convention.]
items.context: Resolution passed by 86 per cent of voting members. Members voting in favour included the Israeli Holocaust historians Raz Segal and Omer Bartov, Hebrew University's Amos Goldberg, and the association's then-president Melanie O'Brien.
items.source: International Association of Genocide Scholars resolution, 31 August/1 September 2025.
items.significance: The determination of the field's own professional body, carried by a supermajority that includes Israeli and Jewish Holocaust historians. It forecloses the argument that the finding is confined to political critics of Israel.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: The overriding principle for applying sovereignty [to the West Bank] is maximum territory with minimum Arabs… There will never, and can never be, a Palestinian state in our land.
items.context: Presenting a plan to annex 82% of the West Bank. In Israeli political usage, “applying sovereignty” means annexation.
items.source: Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post; Crisis Group, “Israel's Quickening Annexation of the West Bank”, October 2025.
items.significance: A demographic formula stated as policy: the maximum land with the minimum number of the protected group on it. This is the definition of ethnic cleansing expressed as a planning principle, attached to a specific territorial percentage.

items.speaker: Hannah Einbinder
items.role: Actor; accepting the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series
items.quote: It is my obligation as a Jewish person to distinguish Jews from the state of Israel. Our religion and our culture is really separate to this sort of ethnonationalist state.
items.context: Said backstage, after closing her acceptance speech with “free Palestine”. The remark drew immediate criticism from Jewish communal organisations, which is recorded here as part of the same fact.
items.source: The Hollywood Reporter; Deadline; NBC News, September 2025. Report §23.4.
items.significance: States the distinction the IHRA examples are most often used to deny — between Jews as a people and the state — made by a Jewish speaker about her own obligations.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: Sovereignty, and also encouraging [Palestinian] voluntary emigration, which we should do also in Judea and Samaria.
items.context: Extending the removal programme explicitly from Gaza to the occupied West Bank.
items.source: Israeli media, September 2025.
items.significance: Direct evidence of intent to forcibly transfer the protected population from the West Bank as well as Gaza, and to annex the territory from which they are removed.

items.speaker: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.role: Navi Pillay (chair), Chris Sidoti, Miloon Kothari
items.quote: On incitement to genocide, the Commission concludes that Israeli President Isaac Herzog, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and then Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, have incited the commission of genocide and that Israeli authorities have failed to take action against them to punish this.
items.context: Report A/HRC/60/CRP.3, presented to the 60th session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva. The Commission also concluded that statements by Israeli authorities are direct evidence of genocidal intent, that the pattern of conduct is circumstantial evidence of it, and that genocidal intent was the only reasonable inference available on the totality of the evidence.
items.source: OHCHR press release and report, 16 September 2025.
items.significance: The first UN body to make an affirmative genocide finding. It expressly noted it had not yet fully assessed statements by Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, and recommended they be assessed for incitement under Article III(c). Israel's ambassador in Geneva called the finding a “libellous rant”.

items.speaker: Yitzhak Wasserlauf
items.role: Minister for the Development of the Negev and Galilee (Otzma Yehudit)
items.quote: The Land of Israel belongs exclusively to the people of Israel — there is no Palestinian people and no Palestinian state.
items.context: Response to the recognition of Palestine by the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.
items.source: Times of Israel; Arab News, September 2025.
items.significance: Denial of the group's existence stated as government position, in direct response to the international community's affirmation of it.

items.speaker: Moshe Ya'alon
items.role: Former IDF Chief of Staff; Minister of Defence, 2013-2016
items.quote: Yeshayahu Leibowitz was right, and I was wrong.
items.context: Written in remarks connected to International Holocaust Remembrance Day, in which Ya'alon said that the “ideology of ‘Jewish supremacy’” had become dominant in the Israeli government and is “reminiscent of the Nazi race theory”. The reference is to the Orthodox Israeli philosopher Yeshayahu Leibowitz (1903-1994) - called “the conscience of Israel” by Isaiah Berlin - who warned from the 1980s that continued occupation would produce what he called “Judeo-Nazis”, and who applied the term to Israeli judges who permitted the torture of Arab detainees.
items.source: Reported February 2026
items.significance: The warning about the dehumanising effect of occupation, made by an Israeli religious philosopher in the 1980s, endorsed four decades later by a former Chief of Staff who had publicly rejected it.

items.speaker: Jewish Federations of North America / Burson
items.role: Survey of more than 1,800 Jewish respondents, fielded March 2025
items.quote: Approximately one third of American Jews identify as Zionist and 7 per cent as anti-Zionist, rising to 14 per cent among those aged 18–34, while nearly nine in ten support Israel’s existence as a Jewish and democratic state and 71 per cent report feeling emotionally attached to Israel.
items.context: The counterweight to the record in Part XXIII. A Washington Post survey of 815 American Jews fielded 2–9 September 2025 (margin of error 4.7 points) found that nearly 40 per cent say Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, that 48 per cent disapprove of its military conduct against 46 per cent who approve, and that 68 per cent hold Hamas more to blame than Israel for civilian deaths.
items.source: Jewish Federations of North America / Burson, published February 2026 (Jewish Insider; JTA; Times of Israel); The Washington Post, September 2025. Report §23.5.
items.significance: Establishes the scale honestly: anti-Zionism is a small minority position among American Jews, criticism of the conduct is not, and the label has lost majority adherence even among supporters of the state.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: [Beirut's southern suburb of Dahiyeh will] soon resemble Khan Younis.
items.context: Stated as the IDF ordered the evacuation of the densely populated southern suburbs of Beirut. Khan Younis had been flattened by more than two years of Israeli bombardment.
items.source: Israeli and Lebanese media, 5 March 2026; Lemkin Institute Red Flag Alert, “Israel in Lebanon”, March 2026.
items.significance: The Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention called it “grotesque” that a state minister would “publicly threaten the Lebanese people with the same large-scale destruction, mass killing, and genocidal violence that has devastated the Palestinians in Gaza.” Proposing to replicate Khan Younis is an admission of what Khan Younis was.

items.speaker: Israel Katz
items.quote: [The IDF will demolish all homes in Lebanese border villages] in accordance with the Rafah and Beit Hanoun model in Gaza.
items.context: Announcing a Gaza-style buffer zone in southern Lebanon and barring the return of “more than 600,000 residents” to areas south of the Litani. Israel proceeded to destroy entire border villages.
items.source: Times of Israel; Common Dreams; Taipei Times, March–April 2026.
items.significance: Naming Rafah and Beit Hanoun as the template is simultaneously an admission of what was done in Gaza and a statement of intent to repeat it against a second population of 600,000.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: Today, the State of Israel changes the rules of the game: anyone who murders Jews will no longer breathe freely or enjoy prison privileges. This is a day of justice for the victims and a day of deterrence for our enemies. No more revolving door for terrorists, but a clear decision. Whoever chooses terrorism chooses death.
items.context: Spoken on the passage of the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law, which Ben-Gvir's party Otzma Yehudit initiated and made a condition of its coalition agreement. The Knesset passed it 62 to 48 at second and third readings after nearly twelve hours of debate; Netanyahu came to the chamber to vote in favour. Ben-Gvir wore a golden noose-shaped lapel pin and handed out champagne afterwards. The law makes death by hanging the default sentence in military courts, which try Palestinians alone, requires execution within 90 days, allows sentencing by a simple majority of judges with no right of appeal, and confines the civilian-track offence to killing aimed at denying the existence of the State of Israel.
items.source: The Times of Israel and The Jerusalem Post, 30 March 2026
items.significance: A minister of the state describing the statutory imposition of capital punishment on one national group as a change in the rules of the game. The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination found on 29 April 2026 that the law is racially discriminatory and an instance of segregation; UN special procedures called it a discriminatory regime of capital punishment. See report section 4.4.

items.speaker: Rossing Center for Education and Dialogue (Federica Sasso)
items.role: Coordinator, Jerusalem Center for Jewish-Christian Relations, at the Israeli organisation that compiles the annual count
items.quote: Year by year, we're noticing a growing normalization of this behavior in public spaces.
items.context: Release briefing for the Rossing Center's 2025 annual report on attacks against Christians in Israel and East Jerusalem, which documented 155 incidents: 61 physical assaults (spitting, hitting and pepper spraying), 52 attacks on church property, 28 cases of verbal harassment (up from 13 in 2024) and 14 defacements of Christian signage. The series records 89 cases in 2023 and 111 in 2024. The report states that all attackers responsible for the tracked spitting incidents, in this period and in previous years, are Jewish, and identifies the perpetrators as drawn mainly from the ultra-Orthodox and national-religious communities.
items.source: Rossing Center, Annual Report 2025; Jerusalem Story, 5 April 2026
items.significance: The count is made by an Israeli organisation, in Israel, of offences committed by Israelis, and is corroborated on an independent methodology by the Religious Freedom Data Center's 181 incidents for the same year, more than 80 per cent of them in Jerusalem. See section 3.5A.

items.speaker: UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination
items.quote: The law marks a grave human rights retrogression and constitutes racial discrimination and segregation against Palestinians, and must be repealed.
items.context: Statement on Israel's Death Penalty for Terrorists Law, released by OHCHR on 1 May 2026. The Committee found that the mandatory sentence operates before military courts with exclusive jurisdiction over Palestinians, that Israeli citizens and residents are excluded, and that the civilian-track offence makes the law de facto applicable to Palestinians only. It called on all States parties to ensure their resources are not used to enforce or support discriminatory policies in the occupied territory, citing the ICJ advisory opinion of 19 July 2024. Israel ratified the Convention in 1979.
items.source: OHCHR press release, 1 May 2026 (statement dated 29 April 2026)
items.significance: A treaty body with jurisdiction over the state, applying the convention the state ratified, finding a statute racially discriminatory on its face. It converts the apartheid analysis at report section 4.2 from inference about administration into a finding about legislation. See report section 4.4.

items.speaker: Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth
items.role: Commander, IDF Central Command (the occupied West Bank)
items.quote: [On why Palestinian stone-throwers are shot dead while Jewish settlers who throw stones at IDF forces are not:] Soldiers' firing on Jews has profound sociological consequences. […] [Asked directly whether this constitutes discrimination:] Yes, it involves discrimination.
items.context: Closed military briefing, leaked to Haaretz. In the same briefing Bluth said “We're killing like we haven't killed since 1967”, and described a deliberate policy of below-the-knee shooting to create “limping monuments” in Palestinian villages.
items.source: Haaretz; Times of Israel, 4 May 2026.
items.significance: The most legally significant self-incriminating admission by an Israeli military official in the public record. The most senior IDF officer in the West Bank conceding that the open-fire policy discriminates by ethnicity — and that the discriminating criterion is whether killing the person would carry “sociological consequences” for the killer's own group — establishes the apartheid character of West Bank enforcement on the occupying power's own evidence.

items.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich
items.quote: The time has come to finally erase the lines that separate Areas A, B, and C.
items.context: Jerusalem Day rally, calling for annexation of the entirety of the West Bank and citing more than a hundred newly approved settlements.
items.source: Jerusalem Post; Chatham House, “Israel's accelerating de facto annexation of the West Bank”, April 2026.
items.significance: The Oslo-era area divisions are the last formal legal acknowledgement that the West Bank is not Israeli territory. Erasing them is annexation by administrative act, prohibited by the peremptory norm against acquisition of territory by force and by the ICJ's July 2024 Advisory Opinion.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: At this point, we are fully in control of 60 percent of the territory of the Gaza Strip… My directive is to move to [70 percent]… Wait, let's go in order. First 70 percent. Let's start with that.
items.context: Filmed remarks at the Ein Prat Leadership Academy. When the audience interrupted, calling for 100 percent, he did not reject the destination — he managed the sequence.
items.source: Al Jazeera; Times of Israel; CNN; Middle East Eye, 28 May 2026.
items.significance: A prime minister already under ICC arrest warrant confirming on camera the seizure of 60% of Gaza beyond ceasefire terms and a directive to reach 70%, in direct defiance of the ICJ's July 2024 order that the occupation end. “First 70 percent” is not a limit; it is a sequence.

items.speaker: Ehud Olmert
items.quote: The State of Israel is conducting an organized, systematic, state-funded campaign of ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity [in the West Bank]. […] These are unprecedented and harsh accusations against the Israeli government and the defense establishment, especially from a former prime minister. But after years of restraint, I have no choice but to make them.
items.context: Column in Haaretz, headlined “Israel Is Conducting a Systematic Campaign of Ethnic Cleansing and Crimes Against Humanity in the West Bank”. He attributed the campaign to “Jewish terrorism” that is “managed, directed, encouraged and supported by the Israeli government.”
items.source: Haaretz, 18 June 2026.
items.significance: A former head of the Israeli government, writing in Israel's newspaper of record, independently reaching the same legal characterisation Amnesty International had reached eight days earlier. The evidentiary weight is exceptional precisely because the speaker cannot be dismissed as an outside critic.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: For every tear of an Israeli mother, a thousand Lebanese mothers must weep. All of Lebanon must burn! […] In the Middle East, you don't win with measured responses and restraint — you need to go berserk. To obliterate. To crush the terror.
items.context: Posted on X following a Hezbollah drone strike that killed four IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon. He added that he had delivered the same message to the Prime Minister “even in our private meetings.”
items.source: Euronews; JNS; Al Jazeera; Middle East Eye; Mediaite; The Daily Caller, 19 June 2026.
items.significance: A serving national security minister calling for an entire country to burn, and proposing a 1,000:1 ratio of Lebanese to Israeli grief, is direct and public incitement to genocide against a second national group under Article III(c). The arithmetic echoes the 50:1 formula articulated by former Military Intelligence chief Haliva in respect of Gaza.

items.speaker: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.role: S. Muralidhar (chair), Chris Sidoti and Navi Pillay — report A/HRC/62/CRP.2, “The essence of childhood has been destroyed”
items.quote: Israeli authorities and security forces have deliberately targeted Palestinian children, amounting to genocide and atrocity crimes in the Gaza Strip and war crimes in the West Bank.
items.context: A hundred-page report covering 7 October 2023 to 31 March 2026, recording at least 20,179 children killed and 44,143 injured, and identifying the Israeli military units responsible for attacks on children. The commission found that children continued to be killed after the October 2025 ceasefire.
items.source: UN Commission of Inquiry, A/HRC/62/CRP.2, 23 June 2026; press conference, Geneva, the same day.
items.significance: The second occasion in the history of UN commissions of inquiry that a dedicated report has been devoted to violations against children, and the commission's second affirmative genocide finding after 16 September 2025. The counter-argument is recorded: UN Watch contends the report fell outside the commission's twice-yearly reporting mandate, which goes to its procedural standing and not to its findings.

items.speaker: Genocide Watch
items.role: Genocide-prevention organisation founded by Gregory Stanton
items.quote: [Gaza is at Stage 8 (Persecution), Stage 9 (Extermination) and Stage 10 (Denial) simultaneously.]
items.context: Assessment against the organisation's Ten Stages of Genocide framework, the model used in US State Department atrocity-prevention training.
items.source: Genocide Watch report, July 2026.
items.significance: The three terminal stages assessed as concurrent. Stage 10, denial, is ordinarily observed only after the killing has stopped; its concurrence with Stage 9 is the analytic counterpart to the statement record in this register, in which extermination is demanded publicly and denied internationally at the same time.

items.speaker: Nachala settler movement march — 28 ministers and MKs
items.role: Serving Israeli government ministers and members of the Knesset
items.quote: Returning home after 21 years.
items.context: At least 28 serving ministers and MKs — nearly half the governing coalition, including Smotrich, Ben-Gvir and Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi — marched to the Gaza border demanding the re-establishment of the settlements of Nisanit, Dugit and Elei Sinai. The IDF declared the area a closed military zone; the ministers marched through it regardless.
items.source: CNN (“Israel's far-right openly boasts of resettling Gaza as election looms”); +972 Magazine; Times of Israel, 19 July 2026.
items.significance: Half a government publicly demanding the resettlement of territory from which 1.9 million Palestinians have been displaced. It is evidence of the specific intent to prevent the return of the protected group and to render the displacement permanent, and would, if executed, constitute the war crime of population transfer into occupied territory.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: The assassinations in Gaza must continue, the encouragement of emigration must happen. Israel must win.
items.context: Posted on X in rejection of the Trump “Board of Peace” Hamas disarmament agreement, which he called “unacceptable to Israel”, adding that a commitment to stop assassinations “is tantamount to agreeing to Hamas organising for the next massacre.”
items.source: Al-Quds; Middle East Eye; France 24; JNS; Times of Israel, 30–31 July 2026.
items.significance: A serving cabinet minister rejecting an internationally brokered agreement precisely because it would end extrajudicial killing and forced emigration, and demanding both as government policy. “Encouragement of emigration” repeats verbatim the euphemism his colleague Karhi has admitted means coerced departure.

items.speaker: Jewish Council of Australia
items.quote: We the undersigned call on governments and institutions around the country to reject the IHRA definition of antisemitism.
items.context: Operative text of the Council's public petition “Don't let Israel define antisemitism”, which describes the definition as “an example of anti-Palestinian racism” that “dangerously conflates Jewish identity with the State of Israel”, and argues that in merging Jews with the Israeli state its examples “only serve to make Jewish people less safe”. It asks institutions to adopt the Australian Human Rights Commission's National Anti-Racism Framework instead, and quotes the definition's drafter, Kenneth Stern, that adoption is “a disaster” because the text is being “weaponised to go after Pro-Palestinian speech… and blind us to how antisemitism actually works”. As at 15 September 2026 it carried more than 26,600 signatures against a target of 30,000.
items.source: Jewish Council of Australia, petition “Don't let Israel define antisemitism”.
items.significance: The same organisation put this analysis to Australia's Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion in June 2026 (§21.5). The petition publishes the Australian adoption record it addresses: AHPRA, the Commonwealth Ombudsman and the Australian Government have adopted the definition; the ABC and SBS have rejected it; ACMA, TEQSA, the Australian Public Service Commission, the Commonwealth Department of Education and most universities have taken no position. See §21.9.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: I think targeted assassinations should be carried out in Gaza, taking down 30 to 40 every night… There are people there who are not worthy of life. They shouldn't live. They're not even people.
items.context: Taped podcast interview with former Gaza hostage Rom Braslavski, surfaced 16–17 August 2026, criticising the drawdown of strikes since the October 2025 ceasefire. He prefaced the remarks: “it's no secret, I disagree with the prime minister.”
items.source: Al Jazeera, 16 August 2026; CBS News; Euronews; ABC News; Truthout, 16–17 August 2026.
items.significance: A serving minister who controls Israel's police and prison services, sitting on the security cabinet, demanding a fixed nightly kill quota during a ceasefire and denying the target population's humanity outright. It is an arithmetic demand for killing, independent of any operational justification. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz condemned the remarks as “dehumanizing” on 19 August 2026. The Lemkin Institute issued a formal statement on 1 September 2026 identifying them as direct incitement to genocide under Article III(c).

items.speaker: Supreme Court of New South Wales (Fagan J)
items.quote: The IHRA proposal is detached from the reality of the common usage and understanding of antisemitism in this country.
items.context: State of New South Wales v Farhat [2026] NSWSC 985, decided 30 July 2026 with reasons published 17 August 2026. The State sought an extended supervision order under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) against Mohommed Farhat over graffiti and arson in Woollahra in November 2024. Fagan J found he had acted as a “vandal for hire” and that the slogans were “crude expressions of political hostility to the state of Israel” rather than hostility to Jews. Deciding that question required the court to decide what antisemitism means; it declined to take the meaning from the IHRA working definition, holding the text “so verbose and imprecise that it could not realistically be attributed to the ordinary, reasonably informed member of the Australian public”, that it “appears to be an attempt to repurpose the term ‘antisemitism’”, and that its effect and evident aim is “to graft onto the community's abhorrence of antisemitism” a “parasitic rejection of protest against Israel”. Reasoning from a June 2026 Pew Research Center survey recording 79 per cent of Australians disapproving of Israel's treatment of the Palestinians, the judgment states that “it would be preposterous to suggest that 79% of Australians are antisemitic because they disapprove of Israel's treatment of the Palestinians.”
items.source: State of New South Wales v Farhat [2026] NSWSC 985, Fagan J; NSW Parliament, 31 August 2026.
items.significance: The rejection of the IHRA working definition is now the reasoned holding of a superior court of record, reached in proceedings brought by a state government against an individual defendant. On 31 August 2026 the New South Wales Attorney General, Michael Daley, told a parliamentary hearing “No, we won't be appealing that decision,” on advice that an appeal had no reasonable prospect of success, so the reasoning stands unappealed. The judgment also holds that “as an ideology of Jewish nationalism, Zionism is open to political discussion and criticism” and that anti-Zionists “hold a negative view of a political ideology” rather than hostility to Jews as Jews. See §21.9.

items.speaker: Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention
items.quote: [Ben-Gvir's call for the deliberate killing of “30 to 40” Palestinians nightly] must be identified as direct incitement to commit genocide under Article III(c) of the 1948 Genocide Convention.
items.context: Formal statement on genocidal incitement by Israel's Minister of National Security. The Institute had earlier issued a Red Flag Alert on Israel in Lebanon (March 2026).
items.source: Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention, 1 September 2026.
items.significance: A genocide-prevention institution applying the Article III(c) standard to a serving cabinet minister's statement within weeks of it being made, during an active ceasefire.

items.speaker: Israel Katz
items.quote: In the end, there is no real solution for Gaza without this migration… [Israel is prepared to achieve it] by sea, by air, and by every way possible… [Trump] has not canceled it; he has frozen it.
items.context: Ynet conference. Katz added that the removal plan is “being discussed all the time”, and “I think that ultimately there is no other solution, for everyone's benefit. But for that to happen, we need the United States, and the moment will come.”
items.source: Times of Israel; Al Jazeera, 2 September 2026; US Senator Chris Van Hollen: “Now the Israeli Minister of Defense confirmed that's the goal.”
items.significance: A serving Defence Minister restating population removal not as a lapsed proposal but as an active plan merely frozen pending US support. On 6 September 2026 the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Türkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE jointly rejected the proposals as a flagrant violation of international law.

items.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir
items.quote: Instead of illusions of peace now, we need actions of emigration now.
items.context: Launch of the ministry programme “Disengagement 710”, ahead of the 27 October 2026 Israeli election: removal of 250,000 Gazans in the first year, 1.11 million within three years, and 1.86 million — the near-totality of the Strip's population — within seven years. He called it “realistic”.
items.source: Al Arabiya; Irish Times; Al Jazeera, 3 September 2026.
items.significance: The conversion of eliminationist rhetoric into a numbered ministry target with a published schedule for the removal of a near-total proportion of a protected group from its territory. Forcible displacement of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; the scale and the timetable are direct evidence of specific intent.

items.speaker: OHCHR
items.quote: [The displacement is] large-scale, long-term and systematic [raising serious concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer.]
items.context: Report finding that Israeli forces forcibly displaced the entire population of the Jenin, Nur Shams and Tulkarem refugee camps during Operation Iron Wall (January–February 2025) — over 33,000 Palestinians — and continue to prevent their return. The use of airstrikes, armoured bulldozers and controlled detonations to render the camps uninhabitable, absent imperative military necessity, also raised concerns of collective punishment and ethnic cleansing. 102 Palestinians, including 21 children, were killed in the period covered.
items.source: OHCHR report, 4 September 2026.
items.significance: A formal UN finding that the crime against humanity of forcible transfer is in issue in the West Bank, independent of Gaza.

items.speaker: Mike Huckabee
items.quote: Crime is crime, terror is terror. […] [There must be] severe consequences.
items.context: Statement on settler attacks at the West Bank village of Turmus Ayya. Huckabee has repeatedly and publicly used the terms “Israeli terrorists” and “horrific acts of terror” of settlement-related violence during 2026, including at Qusra.
items.source: Times of Israel; wire coverage, 5 September 2026.
items.significance: An admission from the government most closely allied with Israel, and from an ambassador with a long record of support for the settlement enterprise, that settler violence meets the definition of terrorism.

items.speaker: Peter Beinart
items.role: Editor-at-large, Jewish Currents; author of Being Jewish After the Destruction of Gaza
items.quote: There's a very legitimate debate about whether you can support a state like that and still have progressive [values].
items.context: A filmed debate published by Zeteo on 9 September 2026 in the Mehdi Unfiltered series, moderated by Mehdi Hasan, against Joel Rubin, a former Obama State Department official and Jewish outreach director of Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaign, who put the opposing case: “Anti-Zionists are clearly hostile to the idea that the state of Israel should exist”, and that for Jews worldwide this crosses a line. Beinart's distinction, in his book, is between the land and the state: “states are not created in the image of God, human beings are. States are merely instruments”.
items.source: Zeteo, “Are Democrats Turning Against Israel – or Jews?”, 9 September 2026. Report §21.8.
items.significance: Recorded with the opposing case stated alongside it. The boundary between criticism of Israel and antisemitism is contested within the community the boundary is drawn to protect, by people who are not outside observers.

items.speaker: Ehud Olmert
items.quote: [Events in the West Bank amount to] no less than attempted ethnic cleansing by a group of murderous criminal terrorists [operating] to harm, steal, destroy, burn and kill Palestinians.
items.context: Radio 103FM, endorsing UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's sanctions announcement. Olmert named Ben-Gvir and Smotrich as the figures who “symbolize this brutal policy… more than anyone else”, alleged the perpetrators number “hundreds of people” with “thousands within the system” providing backing, and warned that IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir could “unjustly become a target for the International Criminal Court”.
items.source: Radio 103FM; Times of Israel, 10 September 2026.
items.significance: The allegation of complicity extending through the army, police and government ministries — not confined to individual settlers — made by a former prime minister on Israeli radio.

items.speaker: Yuval Abraham
items.role: Israeli journalist and co-director of NAZA
items.quote: The Israeli intelligence officers we spoke with talked to us about how this mass killing is systemic: not by accident, but by design.
items.context: Accepting the Special Jury Prize for NAZA at the closing ceremony of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. The film is built on nearly three years of interviews with 24 Israeli soldiers, military intelligence officers and whistleblowers who operated the targeting systems; its title is the Hebrew military acronym for the number of civilians expected to be killed in a strike. Abraham also said: “The denial of a crime is what helps it persist, and that’s why it’s important for us that the Israelis see this film.” The IDF Spokesperson’s Unit categorically rejects the film’s allegations, objecting that the testimonies are anonymous and unverifiable, that they include claims of strategy beyond junior soldiers’ knowledge, and that strike decisions “are made by human personnel only”.
items.source: Venice Film Festival closing ceremony, 12 September 2026; Variety; Deadline; Al Jazeera, 14 September 2026.
items.significance: Testimony from within the targeting apparatus itself, asserting that mass civilian death was designed rather than incidental. If accurate it converges with the Lavender and Habsora reporting of April 2024 and bears directly on the dolus specialis question, since it locates the intent in the operating personnel rather than inferring it from output. The IDF denial is recorded with it.

items.speaker: Miki Zohar
items.role: Minister of Culture and Sport of Israel
items.quote: I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for betraying the state.
items.context: Posted on X after NAZA won the Special Jury Prize at Venice. Zohar called the film “vile” and the award “shocking”, and said that “the self-loathing that burns in the creators, who are willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the world, is inconceivable and constitutes a betrayal of the state”. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called the two a “disgrace and an embarrassment” and told them to leave the country. The Culture Minister holds no power to revoke citizenship: under Article 11(b)(2) of the Citizenship Law, 5712-1952 as amended in 2008, revocation requires an application by the Interior Minister to a court for administrative affairs, on the criteria the Israeli Supreme Court enumerated in Administrative Appeal 8277/17, Zayoud v. Minister of the Interior (21 July 2022) as terrorism, treason or serious espionage, or the acquisition of status in a hostile state. Hebrew sources render the operative phrase as both “betrayal of the state” and “treason against the state”.
items.source: Miki Zohar on X, 13 September 2026; Haaretz, 13 September 2026; Al Jazeera, 14 September 2026; The National; AFP.
items.significance: A serving minister proposing to strip nationality from citizens for documenting the conduct of their own army. Arbitrary deprivation of nationality engages Article 15(2) of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and Article 24(3) of the ICCPR; deprivation for the content of expression additionally engages Article 19 of the ICCPR. It belongs with the record of measures directed at those who document the conduct rather than at the conduct itself.

items.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu
items.quote: We are fighting global anti-Semitic incitement, and when it comes from within us it is intolerable.
items.context: Posted as a video to Telegram on 14 September 2026, two days after the documentary NAZA — built on the testimony of twenty-four anonymous Israeli soldiers and Unit 8200 intelligence officers — won the Special Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Netanyahu called the award “shocking” and objected that “two Israeli directors portraying the [Israeli military] as war criminals receive applause at the Venice festival.” The film's directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, are Israeli citizens, two of the four co-directors of the Oscar-winning No Other Land.
items.source: Benjamin Netanyahu on Telegram, 14 September 2026; Al Jazeera, 14 September 2026; The National, 14–15 September 2026; The Telegraph, 14 September 2026.
items.significance: The testimony the film carries is that of the state's own serving and former personnel, and the answer to it at the head of government is a characterisation of the speakers rather than of what they said. Recorded at §14.1D of the report, with the measures that followed the same day.

items.speaker: Miki Zohar
items.role: Minister of Culture and Sport of Israel
items.quote: Investigate how the materials were obtained, who is behind them.
items.context: Zohar's referral of 14 September 2026, asking the authorities to establish whether the making of NAZA amounted to “aiding the enemy during wartime.” That is a defined offence: section 99 of the Penal Law, 5737-1977 makes a person who, with intent to assist an enemy at war against Israel, commits an act liable to do so “liable to the death penalty or to life imprisonment,” and provides that it is immaterial whether a state of war in fact existed. He separately approached the Interior Ministry, which does hold the revocation power, over the two directors' citizenship.
items.source: Al Jazeera, 14 September 2026; Times of Israel, 14 September 2026; Penal Law 5737-1977, ss. 91, 97–100.
items.significance: The offence proposed against the makers of a documentary is the one Israeli law reserves for assisting an enemy in war, and it carries life imprisonment or death. No application has been filed and the Interior Ministry has not responded. §14.1D.

items.speaker: Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir
items.role: Lieutenant General, Chief of the General Staff of the Israel Defense Forces
items.quote: It is based on blood libels, deliberate distortion of reality, and false and serious accusations.
items.context: Zamir's characterisation of NAZA on 14 September 2026, in remarks in which he also said that he had “not watched the film” and did not know “whom they interviewed in it or who or what is behind it.” In the same instructions he directed the Military Advocate General, Maj. Gen. Itai Ofir, to “examine and advance possible legal actions regarding the film and those involved in it,” ordered an examination of “information security aspects and possible individuals involved in the leaking of classified materials,” and established a Planning Directorate team to develop responses to claims made against the military.
items.source: Times of Israel, 14 September 2026; Ynet, 14 September 2026; Al Jazeera, 14 September 2026; VINnews, 14 September 2026.
items.significance: The Military Advocate General is the office that decides whether to open a criminal investigation into the conduct the twenty-four interviewees describe; it was directed instead at the film and at those involved in it, and the accompanying examination is aimed at identifying the sources. A national apparatus turned on the witnesses rather than on the conduct bears on Article 17 of the Rome Statute. §14.1D.

items.speaker: Hanoch Milwidsky
items.quote: We are not like everyone else, and therefore all the laws that apply to everyone cannot apply to us.
items.context: Speaking on the mission and religious identity of the Jewish people, reported by Israel's Channel 13 and circulated on video from 17 September 2026. In the same remarks he said the land of Israel “was given to us because we are supposed to fulfil a mission here”, that the mission is “to establish a Jewish state here that will be worthy of Jews”, that “the considerations of all kinds of statesmen from around the world should not be relevant to us”, and invoked the biblical “a people that shall dwell alone” (Numbers 23:9) and what he termed “separateness”. The wording is a translation from Hebrew; renderings differ in phrasing between outlets while agreeing on the operative sentence, and no full independently verified English transcript has been published.
items.source: Channel 13, 16–17 September 2026; Anadolu Agency, 18 September 2026; Middle East Monitor, 17 September 2026; Middle East Eye, 19 September 2026.
items.significance: A serving legislator of the governing party asserting that international law does not bind Israel because of the distinctiveness of the Jewish people. Article 27 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties forecloses even the stronger claim, that internal law excuses non-performance of a treaty; the prohibitions of genocide, apartheid and torture are jus cogens and permit no derogation; Common Article 1 of the Geneva Conventions binds parties “in all circumstances”, and Article 2(2) of the Convention against Torture, ratified by Israel in 1991, admits “no exceptional circumstances whatsoever”. Recorded at §15.13A.
